The patient fell ill in the DRC last month and travelled by road to Kampala, Uganda, before flying to Nairobi, where he was taken to hospital and isolated after showing symptoms. Health authorities have identified 28 contacts, including family members and healthcare workers, and are tracing a further 23 passengers and four crew members who were on the same flight. The case has raised questions about how the patient passed health screening while travelling through Uganda and Kenya. Officials say medication may have masked some of his symptoms during screening. Kenya's Health Ministry says the country has the capacity to contain the outbreak and is monitoring those who may have been exposed. 

Al Jazeera's Catherine Soi reports from Nairobi.

description:
Russia and Ukraine have intensified attacks on each other, with large-scale drone strikes targeting Moscow and Russian attacks hitting several Ukrainian cities.

At least two people were killed and seven injured in the Moscow region, according to local authorities, after hundreds of Ukrainian drones were launched overnight. A fuel storage and distribution facility southeast of Moscow was also reportedly hit.

In Ukraine, authorities say Russian attacks killed at least six people and injured dozens in Kharkiv. Strikes also targeted Odesa, where two Ukrainian cargo vessels were destroyed, as well as bridges across the Dnipro River.

The escalation comes as both sides continue targeting infrastructure ahead of winter, while Ukraine has proposed another round of trilateral talks involving Russia and the United States.

Al Jazeera’s Dmitry Medvedenko reports from Moscow and Jonah Hull from Kyiv.
